title: Repeat the Checkout Answer Calmly | Parenting Rewind
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children
education_scope: General parenting education only; not personalised therapy, diagnosis, or medical advice.

narration.transcript: At checkout, a five-year-old may ask for the same treat again in a louder voice after hearing no. Adding a longer explanation each time can accidentally signal that enough questions might change the answer. Pause, move close, and repeat the short direction in the same steady tone. Try: The treat is staying on the shelf; place both hands on the trolley and help me watch for our turn. A consistent answer reduces extra negotiation while a concrete next action shows the child what to do now.

source.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source.title: Tips for Giving Directions
